column2: Three brothers: violin, viola, cello.
One fewer than a quartet. That is why each voice is heard so clearly.
Now, the Mozart Divertimento.
Trio Pasquier: Mozart, Divertimento, K. 563
Father and sons
The Door of Time set a father in his youth and his sons in their maturity in the same rehearsal room.
The sons of Pierre Pasquier — Bruno the violist and Régis the violinist — took up the name of their father's trio.
You two look older than I do.
Father, the way I hold the viola — I have been copying you all my life.
Father, tonight let us play a sextet, with both trios.
Mademoiselle's lesson
The woman called the greatest music teacher of the 20th century, and a violinist of Paris.
Nadia Boulanger was called 'the greatest music teacher of the 20th century' and trained countless fine musicians, composers and performers alike. Her pupils called her, with respect, 'Mademoiselle'.
Régis, there is no hesitation in your sound. But listen to the harmony once more.
Yes, Mademoiselle.
Music lies between discipline and freedom.
24 Caprices
The Devil who wrote the Caprices, and the French virtuoso who recorded them.
Régis Pasquier has recorded all of Paganini's 24 Caprices.
I hear you have played all my Caprices.
I have. Though I did not sell my soul to the Devil.
Ha ha ha! Then it is all the more splendid.
Mozart has died in Vienna, aged 35. The Requiem was left unfinished.
Paganini has died in Nice, aged 57. The Devil's bow has fallen silent at last.
A. Scarlatti: the last opera that never was
Alessandro Scarlatti, father of the Neapolitan school, wrote more than 100 operas and died in 1725.
Marais: Pièces de viole, Book 6
Marin Marais published five books of pieces for the viol. A sixth does not exist in this world.
Gluck: the opera that never was, Hermannsschlacht
In his last years Gluck long planned a Hermannsschlacht on Klopstock's poetry, but no score survives.
Mozart: Requiem, completed by the composer himself
Mozart died at 35 with the Requiem unfinished; his pupil Süssmayr completed it.
Bellini: the next opera that never was
Bellini died at 33, eight months after the premiere of I puritani.
The arias for Malibran that never were
Mezzo-soprano
The diva Maria Malibran died at 28 of injuries from a riding accident.
Field: the nocturnes that never were (new works)
It was the Irish-born Field who created the genre of the nocturne. Chopin inherited the style.
Hummel: the piano concerto that never was
Hummel, a pupil of Mozart, was a pianist ranked alongside Beethoven.
Paganini: the Violin Concerto No. 7 that never was
Paganini's violin concertos are known up to No. 6.
Mussorgsky: Khovanshchina, completed by the composer himself
Bass
Mussorgsky died at 42 with Khovanshchina unfinished; Rimsky-Korsakov completed it.
N. Rubinstein's farewell concert that never was
Nikolai Rubinstein, founder of the Moscow Conservatory, died in 1881 in Paris, where he had gone for his health.
Wagner: the symphony that never was
Wagner tuba
In his last years Wagner said he wished to write symphonies from then on, but he died in Venice in 1883.
Smetana: the symphonic poem that never was
Even after losing his hearing, Smetana completed the cycle of symphonic poems Má vlast.
Rimsky-Korsakov: The Golden Cockerel, premiered by the composer himself
Percussion
His last opera, The Golden Cockerel, was held up by the censor, and its premiere came the year after the composer's death.
Karłowicz: the Violin Concerto No. 2 that never was
The Polish composer Karłowicz died at 32 in an avalanche in the Tatra mountains.
Mahler: Symphony No. 10 (completed by the composer himself)
Viola (the opening monologue)
Mahler died at 50 with his Tenth Symphony unfinished.

Chopin has died in Paris, aged 39. Mozart's Requiem was sung at his funeral.
Chopin: the Piano Concerto No. 3 that never was
Chopin's only piano concertos are the two he wrote around the age of 20. In his last years he had also begun a piano method for his pupils.
Save Chopin from consumption
As his old friend Liszt, stay by him through his last two years.
Paris, January 1848. Chopin is 37, his body eaten away by tuberculosis. In history he dies on 17 October 1849. As his friend, will you stop the journeys that earn him money, or urge him on?

Paris, January 1848.
You are Liszt. Chopin, your friend since youth, has parted from George Sand, and his cough will not stop.
In history he dies on 17 October 1849.

Concerts and journeys fill his purse and his fame but eat away his body. Call an eminent doctor, find a house with good air, and bring him through the night of fate.
The last recital at the Salle Pleyel
His first public concert in six years. The tickets sold out within days. But Chopin can barely climb the stairs.

His sister Ludwika arrives
His sister Ludwika has hurried all the way from Warsaw. For the first time in a long while a smile came to Chopin's face.
Leave brother and sister their time
